title: Split into many ways at once

blocks.text: The page's Q5 splits a range into **N subtasks at once** instead of two, and runs them all at the same time. Its way: fork all the chunks except the last one, compute the last chunk in the current thread, then join the forked chunks (in reverse order).
Its edge cases add: with **more ways than elements**, reduce the number of ways to the number of elements; and with an odd size, one chunk gets the extra elements.
Write `MultiWaySum(array, start, end, ways, threshold, probe)`, a `RecursiveTask<Long>` summing `array[start..end)`:

items: if the range has at most `threshold` elements, or `ways <= 1`, it is a **leaf**: call `probe.leaf(start, end)` once, then sum it sequentially;
otherwise use `w = min(ways, length)` chunks of `length / w` elements each, the **last chunk running to `end`**, and make each chunk a leaf task (`ways = 1`).

blocks.text: The tests also check, in a pool of three workers, that three chunks are all inside `probe.leaf` **at the same time**.

cases.says: The task splits its range into ways chunks and returns their total.
When the length does not divide evenly, the last chunk runs to the end of the range.
With more ways than elements, the ways are reduced to the number of elements, so no chunk is empty.
All chunks but the last are forked before any is joined, so every chunk runs at the same time.
A range [2, 8) is cut into chunks of that range, [2,4) [4,6) [6,8), not chunks counted from index 0.
A range of exactly threshold elements is a single leaf: "at most threshold" includes threshold itself.

concepts: A multi-way split runs all its chunks at the same time; the page forks all but the last, computes the last in the current thread and joins the forked ones.
With an odd or uneven size, one part takes the extra elements.
A multi-way split never uses more ways than there are elements.
